title: W3 exhaustion gate compares timestamps from two different producers with a lexical compare that only works if the byte formats are identical
evidence:
+                      // ISO timestamps — lexical compare is chronological.
+                      string.compare(at, corrected) != order.Lt
...
+       COALESCE((
+         SELECT e->>'at'
+         FROM jsonb_array_elements(rc.attempts) AS e
+         WHERE e->>'detail' = $4 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered'
+         ORDER BY e->>'at' DESC
+         LIMIT 1
+       ), '') AS matched_send_at,
+       -- r1 W3: the correction instant ('' for never-corrected rows).
+       COALESCE(rc.corrected_at::text, '') AS corrected_at,
detail: matched_send_at is an app-written JSON string from the attempts log; corrected_at is Postgres timestamptz::text (space separator, session timezone). If the two formats differ, same-day comparisons misorder: a stale pre-correction bounce could look post-correction and fabricate referee_contact_invalid on a never-retried contact.
recommended_fix: Compare normalized instants (epoch ms or one canonical format) — cast both sides in SQL (e.g. to_timestamp(e->>'at') vs corrected_at) — never raw lexical strings from different producers.

title: Per-slot start re-arms ALL queued rows of the application — rearm_queued_reference_calls ignores the slot filter
evidence:
+  // RC4.3 per-row start: when a slot is requested, keep only that slot —
+  // the other slot is untouched (UX §7.4's per-reference start).
...
+              case sql.rearm_queued_reference_calls(config.db, app_uuid) {
...
+UPDATE reference_call
+SET next_attempt_at = now(),
+    updated_at = now()
+WHERE application_id = $1
+  AND status = 'queued'::reference_call_status
+  AND taken_over_at IS NULL
detail: The slot-filtered create leaves sibling slots untouched, but the re-arm UPDATE is application-scoped: a per-slot start forces every queued row to due-now, collapsing sibling slots' staged cadence — contradicting per-slot semantics added in the same diff.
recommended_fix: Scope the re-arm by ref_slot when a slot filter is supplied (add a slot parameter to rearm_queued_reference_calls), or deliberately re-arm-all and document it.

title: Re-arm side effect also fires on the suppressed (declined) start path
evidence:
+        Some("declined") -> Ok(Suppressed)
...
+            Ok(_) -> {
+              // r1 (W6): "Start this check now" on an application whose
+              // rows already exist (the auto-trigger created them) is an
+              // insert no-op — the honest re-arm nudges every queued row to
+              // due-now so the sweep picks them up on the next tick (the
+              // §7.4 promise "sends the invite now"). Best-effort.
+              case sql.rearm_queued_reference_calls(config.db, app_uuid) {
detail: run_create_checks_slot returns Ok(Suppressed) for declined applications, which matches Ok(_): the re-arm still nudges any queued rows to due-now and the API reports started. A suppressed start should be side-effect-free.
recommended_fix: Match Ok(Suppressed) explicitly in run_start_action and skip the re-arm (and consider whether 'started': true is honest for a suppressed start).

title: Archived-vacancy precheck fails open on query error or empty result
evidence:
+    Ok(pog.Returned(_, [vacancy_row])) if vacancy_row.is_archived ->
+          response_helpers.json_error(
+            error_code.VacancyUnavailable,
+            "This vacancy is archived. Restore it to continue reviewing applications.",
+            422,
+          )
+        _ -> action()
detail: Only Ok(Returned([row])) with is_archived true blocks; an Error from verify_vacancy_active (or 0 rows) falls through to '_' and the mutation executes. A failed availability check should abort, not proceed.
recommended_fix: Handle Error/empty explicitly — 500 on query error, 422/404 on missing vacancy — before running action().

title: update_trio's unknown-slot arm fabricates a bogus pog.UnexpectedArgumentCount error
detail: An unexpected ref_slot produces a 500 log ('unexpected argument count') describing nothing real. The defensive arm should return a domain-meaningful error instead of a synthesized pog error.
recommended_fix: Add an UnknownSlot variant to ActionError (or reuse NotSubstitutable) and map it to a 409/500 with honest logging.

title: Idempotent substitute no-op still re-stamps creation fraud on the pre-existing successor row
evidence:
+                  "existing" -> Ok(new_row.id)
...
+    Ok(new_id) -> {
+      // r1 (N1): the new row gets the same creation-time fraud screening the
+      // viewed trigger applies (parity — best-effort, post-commit).
+      trigger.stamp_creation_fraud_for(
+        config,
+        app_uuid,
+        landlord_uuid,
+        vacancy_uuid,
+        [new_id],
+      )
detail: The 'existing' path is documented as a no-op ('the original did both'), yet stamp_creation_fraud_for still runs on the successor id — re-running creation-time screening on a row already stamped at its own creation and possibly progressed.
recommended_fix: Return the how flag from do_substitute and skip stamp_creation_fraud_for when how == 'existing'.

title: do_correct ignores update_trio's row count — a 0-row trio UPDATE still commits the audit and returns 200
evidence:
+                case
+                  update_trio(tx, app_uuid, vacancy_uuid, row.ref_slot, trio)
+                {
+                  Error(err) -> Error(DbFailure(err))
+                  Ok(_) ->
detail: The W10 fix closed the cross-vacancy 0-row at the precheck, but the in-transaction trio UPDATE result is still discarded: if the application row vanishes between precheck and tx, the audit records a correction that never landed.
recommended_fix: Treat Ok(0) from update_trio as a rollback error (no audit, honest 5xx), mirroring correct_reference_call's 0-row handling.
